newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Most Israelis favour peace moves after bombing.
newsitem.headline: Most Israelis favour peace moves after bombing.

text.p: Two-thirds of Israelis favoured renewing peacemaking with Palestinians eight days after suicide bombers blew up a Jerusalem market, an opinion poll showed on Friday.
The Dahaf Institute poll of 501 Israelis, taken on Thursday, showed 66 percent favoured renewing the peace process while 32 percent wanted to halt it and two percent had no response.

The poll, for the Yedioth Ahronoth newspaper, also showed 71 percent of Israelis backed a closure on Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza imposed by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government following the July 30 bombing.
The poll had a margin of error of four percent.
The two suicide bombers blew up the Israeli Mahane Yehuda market, taking the lives of 13 people with them.
Netanyahu suspended peace talks with the Palestinians after the bombing. He says the Palestinians must crack down on militants before negotiations can resume.
The Palestinians say they have fought militants despite having stopped security cooperation with Israel in March when it launched a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
